_doc: RFC_029 §10.15 — the `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT marker on ExtractActionInputs' step-config surface (council REVISE round 1, bug_historian's gating objection). A `?` wire resolves its declared path OR LEAVES THE FIELD ABSENT, deliberately with no error, no log and no row: absence is the contract. Nothing at runtime can tell an intended absence from a mistyped path, so the guard is offline and fleet-wide — `config-key-audit --optional-explicit-wires` lists every live `?` wire and exits 1 on any that is not acknowledged here. An entry records that a human READ THE DOWNSTREAM CODE of the consuming action and confirmed it treats an absent field as a safe no-op, rather than as an empty string or zero it will render or persist. `downstream` is not optional in spirit: an entry with an empty statement is ignored (and warned about), because an ack that says nothing about what was checked is precisely the hollow ack the objection named. Key shape is `<action>.<field>` — keyed on the ACTION, because coping-with-absence is a property of the code that consumes the field, not of which workflow wired it. Sibling file and precedent: optional_key_budget_acks.json (RFC_022).
_first_adopters: The marker shipped with ZERO adopters (v1.0.1321, live 2026-08-20). Entries are added WITH the migration that wires them — if you are adding a `?` wire, the acks entry belongs in the same commit, the way a _HOLD migration travels with its reason; otherwise the gate goes red on someone else's clock. Live as of 2026-08-21: plan_sections.page_type (migration 515, applied), create_tool_component.replace_existing (532, applied — PROVISIONAL, awaiting its owner). Not yet live: the two related_pages entries (516, HELD behind migration 512's demand control). COUNT IS NOT PINNED HERE ON PURPOSE — this line goes stale the moment someone adds a wire, so trust `config-key-audit --optional-explicit-wires` over it; it reads the live fleet, this sentence reads whatever was true when it was typed.

plan_sections.page_type.downstream: plan_sections_action.go:972-975 reads `pageType := inputs.Get("page_type")` and, when it is empty, falls back to the page's own NAME (`pageType = pageName`) for the component-selector scoring bonus; the comment at :968-970 states the selector still works without it, just without site/page-type relevance bonuses. So absence degrades scoring on that one axis and cannot render or persist an empty value. It is also strictly better than today's alternative on the 18/31 runs where the page's own record is missing from the tree: without the marker the ONLY candidates are OTHER pages' page_type, so absence replaces a foreign value with a locally-correct one.

create_tool_component.replace_existing.downstream: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-21 ~17:0xZ (the bugs_open/286→331 session, author of the wire, TL-047 and migrations 496+532) — the provisional text below is accurate and is retained; what the owner CHECKED, first-hand, at HEAD and live: (1) the sole reader is replaceExistingRequested (create_tool_component_regenerate.go), which is GetBool('replace_existing', false) plus an EqualFold on the quoted string 'true' — absent resolves to false and the regenerate arm is never entered, before any read or write of the incumbent; (2) pinned by test arm A (TestCreateToolComponent_ReplaceAbsentKeepsTheAlreadyExistsShortCircuit — the sqlmock walk ENDS at the probe, zero writes); (3) proven LIVE post-532 by a SECOND producer: add_tool item 4531f29c-7630-4769-b05e-c0e7ff569d23 (tool-jwt-inspector, 13:58:49Z, spec verified to carry NO replace_existing key) built cleanly through save_tool. So absent ⇒ the already_exists short-circuit or a plain creation, exactly as before 496. | PROVISIONAL TEXT AS ROUTED (accurate): Absence is not merely safe here, it is the ONLY correct behaviour and it is pinned: TL-047 records 'absent ⇒ byte-identical (pinned)' at the action layer, and CreateToolComponentInputSpec's own comment states 'absent ⇒ today's path' (the already_exists short-circuit). This wire exists BECAUSE absence broke: migration 496 wired it strictly (`replace_existing!`) at 12:12Z, which fails extraction outright when the field is missing. MECHANISM vs MEASURED DAMAGE, kept apart: the mechanism kills EVERY plain add_tool (one with no replace_existing in its spec) at save_tool while its work item reads `complete` with error NULL; the measured damage over the 98-minute window is exactly ONE item fleet-wide (item cd3812b5, ~13:40Z, `strict '!' fields did not resolve: [replace_existing]`), across 5 orchestration ATTEMPT rows — attempt-level and item-level counting differ and both are true, so cite 'one item, fleet-wide'. 532 converted it to `?` at 13:50:42.682761Z precisely to keep the search exclusion while allowing absence. Both arms proven behaviourally the same hour (finder's first-hand measurements): refile 298fa5f8 with an explicit `replace_existing: false` built clean PRE-fix, and item 4531f29c (13:58:49Z, no key at all) built clean POST-fix, followed by two more plain-absence builds (09d63a2f, e947d58a). So the downstream question this ack exists to ask was answered in production, in the hard direction, on the same day.

create_tool_component.related_pages.downstream: Read first-hand 2026-08-21. Both tool build actions reach one helper, relatedPagesFromInputs (create_tool_cross_link_items.go:443, called from create_tool_component_action.go:527 and deploy_tool_action.go:271,548): with the field absent, GetRaw returns nil and it re-reads the SAME declared path directly, which is also nil, so absence propagates and nothing reaches for a search. Absence is then INSTRUMENTED rather than merely tolerated (create_tool_cross_link_items.go:142-151): `if len(req.relatedPages) == 0` logs at info and records a counted skip with reason `no_related_pages` and the comment 'Not a defect: a suggestion may legitimately name no related pages', then returns 0 — emitting no cross-link items. Emitting none is the CORRECT behaviour for a spec that names no related pages, and is the whole point of bugs_open/330: the value being substituted today is another tool's.

deploy_tool_to_site.related_pages.downstream: Same helper, same absence path, same instrumented skip as create_tool_component.related_pages above — deploy_tool_action.go:271 and :548 both call relatedPagesFromInputs. Recorded separately because the ack is keyed on the CONSUMING action and a future change to one action's absence handling must not be vouched for by the other's entry. Note this step has ZERO logged conflict rows: its inclusion in 516 is prophylactic (an identical unmarked wire to identical code), stated as such in the migration.

complete_work_item.commit_sha.downstream: Read first-hand 2026-08-21 at load_work_item_actions.go:937: `if sha := inputs.Get("commit_sha"); sha != "" { resultData["commit_sha"] = sha }`. Absent means the key is simply NOT WRITTEN into the work item's result — no empty string is persisted and nothing downstream is handed a blank. The value is also not lost when absent from this field: the sibling `result!` mapping puts the WHOLE handler_result into `result`, and that envelope still carries the sha at the handler's own path, so the top-level copy is a convenience duplicate rather than the only record. Absence is additionally the CORRECT outcome on runs that genuinely produced no commit — measured on live traffic: of 31 recent bdl runs carrying a handler_result, 2 had none (a page-build-handler early exit whose response held only site_record, and a page-rerender whose deploy_result produced no commit). Today those 2 are handed an arbitrary sha by the whole-tree search, sometimes from a DIFFERENT work item in a different loop iteration (worked case: item cc1db035). So for this field, absence is not merely safe — it is the repair.

store_generated_component.advised_identi.downstream: store_generated_component_action.go reads it as `advisedIdentityPin(inputs.GetRaw("advised_identity"))`. ABSENCE IS READ, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT IS A REAL NO-OP: GetRaw returns nil, the type assertion to map[string]interface{} fails, the helper returns ("", "") and the `if advisedID != ""` branch is not entered — control falls to the else, which is the pre-388 call `resolveStorageIdentity(ctx, params.DB, functionName, requesterSiteID, requesterDomain, logger)`, byte-identical to what shipped before this key existed. No empty string is stored, rendered or compared: the value is a component UUID used solely to choose WHICH ROW a regeneration overwrites, and an empty one selects no row rather than a wrong one. A malformed value is also handled rather than trusted — advisedIdentityPin shape-checks the id (8-4-4-4-12 hex) and degrades to the same legacy path if it fails, so a mistyped path that somehow resolved to a non-UUID string cannot reach Postgres as a cast error on a write that had a working fallback. THE MARKER IS LOAD-BEARING HERE RATHER THAN CONVENTIONAL: without the `?` this key would be eligible for the aggressive whole-tree search, and a field that decides which shared component row gets overwritten must resolve from its declared path or not at all — a plausible-but-wrong match would silently redirect a write. Verified by test: the four pinned-path tests in component_storage_identity_test.go supply the wire explicitly, and the pre-existing un-pinned tests (ForeignCollisionDivertsToCreation, OwnSiteCollisionRegenerates, UnknownRequesterKeepsLegacyRefusal, SilentParallelBirthIsRecorded) supply nothing and still pass unchanged under sqlmock, which fails on any unexpected statement — so the absent case is exercised on every run, not merely argued.
